correctness.rationale: Path multiplication forces the semisimple coefficients to vanish, yields a_i a_{i+1}=0 and a_i b_{i+1}+b_i a_{i+2}=0, with free length-three coefficients. For each cyclic independent support, row/column incidences of the b-system form disjoint stars and rank is 2s−t2−t3 in every characteristic. Disjoint-support counting gives the theorem; the five-state transfer determinant proves its recurrence with direct initial values. Standalone independent multiplication and finite-field rank checks passed (11 configurations), and transfer/recurrence calculations passed on 6 sizes × 13 lengths. Finite checks are supplementary to proof.

value.rationale: Counting all square-zero elements is a standard natural arithmetic invariant of a finite-dimensional associative algebra. In J⁴ cyclic Nakayama algebras the constraint includes a genuinely new nontrivial coupled b-equation absent in shorter truncations. The support-dependent rank identity collapses the coupling into a five-state transfer and a fourth-order recurrence valid uniformly for every finite field and unbounded cycle length, rather than a single computed example or known-table repetition.
